chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Halab (Al-Halabi) from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Any man who makes a vow to walk to the House of Allah (the Sacred Kaaba) and then becomes unable to walk, let him ride and sacrifice a camel, when Allah knows effort from him.

key_terms.بَدَنَةً: a camel (specifically a female camel used for sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What is the substitute for a Hajj vow if one cannot walk on foot?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) regarding the flexibility in fulfilling vows (*nadhr*) when physical incapacity arises. The Imam clarifies that if one vows to walk to the Kaaba but cannot, they may ride and offer a camel (*badanah*) as expiation, provided they exerted their utmost effort (*al-jahd*) in attempting the original vow. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*taysir*) in religious obligations when circumstances change.
